sections.heading: A system that fits your kitchen
paragraphs: Every kitchen has its own equipment layout, available space and route for extraction. We design and install ventilation systems that bring the canopy, ductwork and fan together around these requirements.

The installation shown here places the canopy directly above the cooking line, alongside the surrounding metal wall panels. Reviewing the equipment positions and site measurements helps establish how each part of the extraction system will fit.
sections.alt: Kitchen extraction canopy with filter panels above a cooking line and patterned metal wall cladding.

sections.heading: Considered from the kitchen to the exterior
paragraphs: The ductwork route is an essential part of planning a kitchen ventilation installation. Available space, changes of direction and the points where ductwork passes through the building all need to be considered together.

This exterior view shows a rectangular duct section with a formed transition at its base. Our service covers ductwork design and fabrication, fan installation and commissioning. For a quotation, send a kitchen plan and photographs of the proposed route.
sections.alt: External rectangular metal duct with a formed transition section beside a tiled roof.

sections.heading: Canopies made for the working space
paragraphs: The size and position of an extraction canopy should reflect the appliances beneath it and the space around them. We supply and install stainless steel canopies to suit the dimensions and arrangement of a commercial kitchen.

The photograph shows a canopy running above a cooking line, with filter panels and lighting visible underneath. Equipment positions, ceiling height and access to the filters are considered when reviewing the installation.
sections.alt: Extraction canopy with filter panels and lights above a line of vertical cooking units.

sections.heading: A careful fit around the room
paragraphs: Canopy sections often meet wall panels, corners and openings within the same space. The view here shows these elements brought together around a kitchen serving hatch, with the metalwork following the corner of the room.

We review measurements and the ductwork connection before confirming the canopy specification. Fabrication and fitting are coordinated with the kitchen layout, followed by balancing and testing of the extraction system.
sections.alt: Corner canopy sections and metal wall cladding fitted around a kitchen serving hatch.

sections.heading: A practical finish for working kitchens
paragraphs: Wall cladding gives cooking, preparation and washing areas a durable, wipeable surface. We fabricate and fit stainless steel panels to the dimensions of the room, taking account of the equipment and services already in place.

This installation uses patterned metal panels around a sink and adjoining wall. The repeating surface finish continues across the corner, while the panel edges follow the boundaries of the working area.
sections.alt: Patterned metal wall cladding continuing around a corner above a kitchen sink.

sections.heading: Panels planned around the details
paragraphs: Door openings, corners and service points shape the layout of a cladding installation. Panel sizes, joints and returns are planned together so the finished metalwork fits the space and meets the surrounding surfaces.

The second view shows the patterned cladding around a doorway beside kitchen equipment. Share wall dimensions, photographs and the positions of any fittings when enquiring, together with your preferred finish or details of existing panels.
sections.alt: Patterned metal wall panels fitted around a doorway beside kitchen equipment.

sections.heading: Made around the way your space works
paragraphs: The right dimensions and arrangement make a difference to how equipment fits within a kitchen. We manufacture stainless steel tables, sinks and canopies to an agreed specification, with bespoke fabrication and welding for individual requirements.
This central kitchen pass combines work surfaces with an overhead frame and lighting. The view shows the relationship between the metal tops, upright supports and surrounding preparation space.
sections.alt: Metal kitchen pass with work surfaces, upright supports and lights in the overhead frame.

sections.heading: Details agreed before fabrication
paragraphs: We work from drawings and measurements to establish the size, layout and finish of each piece. Joints, edges, openings and clearances are considered alongside the equipment and surfaces the new metalwork will sit beside.

The wider view shows the central pass in place between the cooking line and open shelving. To discuss a similar fabrication requirement, send the overall dimensions and a sketch or photographs of the area, including any essential connections or access points.
sections.alt: Long central kitchen pass between a cooking line with extraction canopies and open metal shelving.
